sections.overview: Tramea carolina is a skimmer dragonfly of eastern North America.
sections.identification: Males have a red face and abdomen, metallic-violet forehead and dark reddish hindwing patches. Unlike T. onusta, the male has violet on the forehead.
sections.habitat: It uses ponds, lakes, marshes and slow streams, including temporary ponds.
sections.diet: Adults feed while flying over open areas; the cited state account does not specify their prey.
sections.behavior: Males patrol shorelines and may perch on twigs; northward migration is possible but uncertain.
sections.reproduction: Mating occurs in vegetation, followed by egg deposition among emergent plants.
sections.ecology: Like T. insularis, it belongs to Tramea; the checklist places T. insularis farther south, mainly in the southern United States, Mexico and the West Indies.
sections.conservation: The Wisconsin account gives a global rank of G5; this broad rank does not show that every local population is secure.
